thread:
Alex: Heads up — we just hit a multi-node TP hang on the 8xA100 cluster during nightly perf runs. root cause looks like rank desync after an all-reduce at step 42.

Jia: ugh. which model and which kernel path?

Alex: redwood/gptx-13b-quant, tensor+pipeline parallel enabled. Kernel selection switched to fused-attn-v2 at runtime. Logs show a timeout waiting on `nccl:AllReduce` on rank 2.

Sam: can you paste the relevant stack/log lines?

Alex: sure — excerpt: ```
[2025-10-12T03:14:22Z] Rank 2: NCCL_CALL(allReduce) -> timeout after 210000 ms
[2025-10-12T03:14:22Z] Rank 2: last op op_id=9876 stage=kv_cache_flush
[2025-10-12T03:14:22Z] Rank 2: local queue drained, waiting for peer rings
[2025-10-12T03:14:22Z] Rank 2: heartbeat lost for peer 5
```

Jia: that `kv_cache_flush` in the log is suspicious — we recently changed the KV cache eviction to synchronous flush on pipeline boundary for smaller memory footprints. Might be blocking comm.

Matt: I also see from perf profile that comm/compute overlap dropped to 5% on node 2: ```
# perf summary
node0: compute 72% comm 22% overlap 34%
node2: compute 60% comm 30% overlap 5%
```

Devon: If overlap goes to 5% we will get stalls. Are we forcing a different NCCL algorithm/threshold when fused-attn-v2 is used? That can change message sizes and trigger ring-chunking.

Alex: Good point. Kernel selection picks kernels based on sequence length distribution — for this run sequence=1024, we chose the large-LL threshold and ran contiguous KV writes which increased the single-op message size to ~120MB.

Sam: 120MB all-reduce per step plus synchronous KV flush sounds like collision. Maybe rank 2 hit network jitter and lost a heartbeat. infra-bot will have NIC counters.

infra-bot: NIC alerts: node2 eth0: 3 rx_err, 1 tx_err within 5m window. GPU pci-e errors: none. Link speed: 100Gbps.

Jia: Nice — hw noise. Two things to try: 1) revert KV flush to async (buffered) for pipeline boundary, 2) force NCCL algorithm to ring for >64MB so chunking is predictable.

Alex: I rolled a canary patch to run buffered KV flush on node2 only (via local env override) — starting a run now. thread id: run-525.

Matt: while that's running, can we capture traces? Use our perf probe: `rdw-perf trace --pid <runner> --ncclevents --kv` and push to s3.

Devon: also adjust batching heuristic: reduce micro-batch size from 8->4 for TP pipeline stage 1 to lower peak message size. Might increase compute overhead but reduce per-step comm.

Sam: run-525 trace uploaded: s3://ci-traces/run-525/trace.json. Quick grep: all-reduce sizes dropped to ~48MB, overlap improved to 31% on node2, no NCCL timeouts but occasional 100ms gap spikes.

Alex: results look promising. No hangs so far, last_message_ts matches run end. But we still see 100ms rx spikes. infra-bot: any further NIC issues?

infra-bot: post-run NIC stats: node2 eth0: rx_err 0, tx_err 0 in last 10m. rx_unicast dropped from 1.2M->1.1M. No hardware resets.

Jia: OK so combined mitigation worked: buffered KV flush + smaller micro-batch + NCCL ring override. We should make this a temporary policy when sequencing>512 and multi-node TP enabled.

Matt: agree. Also we need an automagic profiler rule: if comm/compute overlap < 10% for a rank AND all-reduce sizes > 80MB, trigger soft-fallback to alternate kernel or reduce batch.

Devon: I can prototype a scheduler heuristic: compute per-rank comm budget = target_latency * avg_throughput; if estimated all-reduce > budget then switch to chunked ring or lower micro-batch.

Sam: Will be important for Dedicated customers with mixed noisy neighbors. Add added telemetry: per-rank NCCL op sizes, KV cache flush latency, and hardware err counters.

Alex: I'll open a follow-up PR with the buffered-kv change + NCCL env knobs + a perf alert for overlap <10%. Assigning to Jia and Devon for heuristic and Matt for alerting.

Jia: assigned. I'll also document the kernel-selection edge-case where fused-attn-v2 increases comm footprint for long sequences.

Matt: Thanks. Postmortem-ish notes: root cause = synchronous KV flush + large all-reduce messages + transient NIC jitter -> rank desync/timeouts. Mitigation = buffering KV flush, reduce micro-batch, enforce ring-chunking for big messages, profiler alert.

Alex: closing the ticket for now — will reopen if run-526 hangs. :thumbsup:

Devon: one last note: add a unit test that simulates per-rank delay to catch hangs earlier (mock NCCL with artificial latency).

Sam: good idea. I'll add a CI job that runs the multi-node hang sim nightly on a 4-node emu.

Alex: thanks everyone.
